title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Saturn
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3, Book III chapter 1 and Book III chapter 8

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Saturn, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his weight and his cold. Saturn holds the power of retention, and when he is afflicted he is the gravest of the impediments: the science of law and profound knowledge, deep and occult properties, the building trades, and working the soil are his, with murky rivers, black mountains, deep wells, and desert places among his locations. Lead and iron are his metals, black his color, the bitter taste his own. Well disposed and direct, he gives purity, long life, standing, honor, riches, and durable inheritances; afflicted, he is the lord of poverty, misery, pain, and imprisonment.
